versions.title: Crash notices, Ocarina of Time options, tidier save folders
new: RetroHub now tells you when an emulator stopped unexpectedly or could not start. The note has buttons to open the crash file folder and the emulator's log, and to copy the details. It waits until you are back in RetroHub and never appears over a game

Ocarina of Time on Fritchii has three new options in the game's settings: high refresh rate (experimental, above 60 fps at normal game speed), its frame rate cap, and anti-aliasing. Left alone, they keep Fritchii's own settings
fixed: Looking at a game no longer creates empty battery and states folders for it in the save vault. Folders that already exist are left alone

versions.title: Ocarina of Time: shader preparation crash fixed
fixed: Ocarina of Time (Switch 2) on Fritchii v5.7 no longer crashes while it prepares shaders. Press Play and choose Update to get the repaired Fritchii
Preparing shaders carries on from where it stopped; it does not start over

versions.title: Fritchii v5.7 for Ocarina of Time
new: Ocarina of Time (Switch 2) now plays with Fritchii v5.7. Press Play and choose Update to get it
In Fritchii you can press Ctrl+U in Ocarina of Time to go above 60 fps at normal game speed (experimental), and again to go back
improved: Fewer hitches: no more freezes of up to 3 seconds when the game swaps a shader, less stutter right after you enter a new area, and shorter pauses on loads
Less memory: graphics memory stays around 6 GB instead of climbing to 10 GB, and PCs with 16 GB of RAM no longer run out of memory
The opening cutscenes and the main menu video stay in sync with their sound
fixed: Stretched or glowing geometry and the huge glowing triangles that could build up over a long session should be gone or much rarer
Two missing objects in Kakariko graveyard are drawn again
The Song of Time no longer ends with a loud crackle, and opening the ocarina without a microphone no longer crashes the game
After the update, Preparing shaders runs once more before the game starts. Let it finish: the game runs worse while it is still preparing

versions.title: Lichii build 130: faster Ocarina of Time, less memory
improved: Switch games on Lichii now use Lichii build 130. Ocarina of Time runs faster on it (about 25% in Lichii's own measurements), Lichii uses about 6 GB less memory, and it no longer keeps a whole CPU core busy while it waits

Lichii's new shader cache builds far fewer shaders again when you come back to a game. Your existing cache is converted the first time you start a game after the update: with a big cache that one start can take longer and use a few GB of memory for a moment
To get it, press Play on a Switch game and choose Update. Your saves, settings and keys are not touched. Ocarina of Time still starts with Fritchii unless you picked Lichii for it
fixed: Closing a Switch game: when Lichii gets stuck while closing, RetroHub now waits until it has finished writing its shader cache before ending it

versions.title: Nintendo Switch 2 on its own
new: Nintendo Switch 2 is its own console everywhere: badges, filters, groups, settings, controllers and stats
improved: Home: Favorites now come first, and "Jump back in" is now "Recently played"
PS4/PS5/Switch Pro controllers: the D-pad works in Switch games without rebinding
fixed: Pressing buttons in a game no longer clicks things in RetroHub behind it (e.g. the folder picker popping up)
Damaged-file repair now also fixes broken sound files (e.g. a missing voice line in Ocarina of Time), not just textures

versions.title: Play time, Steam style
new: Every game page shows how long you have played, like Steam: "42.6 hours played" and the day you last played it, right under the title, plus a small strip with your play time, last played, sessions and hours in the last 2 weeks
Play time counts every PC you play on. When another PC played the game too (its play log syncs with your saves), the strip shows how much was played on this PC and how much on the others
Sorted by Most played, the library shows each game's hours on its tile ("12.5 hours", or "Not played yet"), and in the Cases view the hours lead the line under the centred game
improved: The list view's Play time column and the Showcase view show play time in hours, the same way as the game page

versions.title: Fritchii v5.5, and damaged game files repaired automatically
new: Ocarina of Time plays with Fritchii v5.5. RetroHub's build of it now runs as Fritchii itself, so its Preparing shaders screen appears when the game starts and prepares every shader at full speed before you play (about 10 to 15 minutes, once after this update), instead of in the background while you play

Switch games in .nup files: when you press Play, RetroHub now checks the copy for damaged files and fills each one in with a matching intact file from the same copy. Some copies of Ocarina of Time have a few blank files that make whole rooms invisible, like the Water Temple walls, the fairy fountain caves and part of Ganon's Castle. Your game file is never changed, and you can turn this off with Repair damaged game files in the game's Settings tab
improved: Fritchii v5.5 keeps a large NVIDIA shader cache for itself, fixes dialogue text that could show scraps of other textures, and fits its windows to Windows' display scale
The game page says when a copy has damaged files and which places they affect. Only a fresh dump of your own copy restores them exactly
fixed: Ocarina of Time: the Water Temple walls show up again on copies with a damaged wall texture
Ocarina of Time lagged while Fritchii prepared its shaders in the background during play

versions.title: Fritchii v5 for Ocarina of Time
new: Ocarina of Time now plays with Fritchii v5 by default. The first time, a Preparing shaders screen builds the game's shaders once (about 10 to 15 minutes); after that, new areas load without shader stutter. Other Switch games keep Lichii, and you can pick Lichii for Ocarina in its Settings tab
improved: Fritchii v5 uses less memory and runs the heaviest Ocarina of Time areas, like the Water Temple, more smoothly
NVIDIA tip: set Shader Cache Size to Unlimited in the NVIDIA Control Panel (Manage 3D settings) so the prepared shaders are kept
fixed: The incomplete game file warning no longer flags complete copies: it only appears when the file itself shows it was cut short

versions.title: Recently used shaders by default
improved: Shaders at start now defaults to Recently used on every PC: Switch games start quickly and use much less memory, and new shaders are built as you play. Pick Auto or All cached shaders in Settings if you prefer

versions.title: Faster GPU reads for Switch, start animation and menu sounds off
new: New Switch setting Faster GPU reads, on by default: Lichii no longer waits for the GPU every time a game reads graphics memory back, which can make parts of Ocarina of Time much faster. If something looks wrong in a game, turn it off in Settings or in the game's Settings tab
improved: Switch games start much faster on PCs with less than 64 GB of memory: Shaders at start on Auto now builds the shaders you used recently instead of every cached one (a big Ocarina of Time cache could take minutes, and much longer right after a Lichii update). Pick All cached shaders to get the old behaviour
The game start animation and all menu sounds are turned off for now
The incomplete game file warning now only shows on the game's page, next to its description. It no longer pops up when you press Play, and Library health no longer lists it

versions.title: Clearer online endings and steadier Game Boy clocks
fixed: If the host's game crashes or their PC drops off during an online game, the other players are now told the host left instead of "Connection lost"

Game Boy games that keep their own clock (like Pokémon Crystal ROM hacks) now use SameBoy in online rooms even if you picked Gambatte, because Gambatte can't keep that clock in step between PCs. The host sees a short note when this happens

versions.title: Lichii build 125 and a warning for incomplete game files
new: RetroHub now warns you when a Switch game file looks incomplete or cut short. An incomplete copy can be missing walls or textures in some areas, like Ocarina of Time's Water Temple. The warning shows on the game's page, in Library health, and once before you play
improved: Lichii (Switch) is updated to build 125. It can build some shaders that build 95 couldn't, so some missing graphics may now show up. Shaders preloaded at start now stay loaded until they're used, and your shader cache carries over. Press Play on a Switch game and choose Update
Lichii's own update check and updater are switched off: RetroHub keeps Lichii up to date

versions.title: Signed updates, safer saves and smoother online play
new: Updates are now signed: RetroHub checks every update against the publisher's signature before it installs anything
Smaller updates: when only RetroHub changed, it updates without downloading Smash Classic again
Hide a game from Customize or its details. A new Show hidden filter lists hidden games, dimmed, with an Unhide button
Game night reminders arrive as a Windows notification 10 minutes before the start, even when RetroHub is closed (turn on Windows notifications in Settings; never shown while you play)
The game menu (View + Y) now works in GameCube online games: volume, screenshot and leave (or hold Back + Start)
Dolphin's game menu can pause the game and quick-save or quick-load (slot 1) in offline games
Use host's save now also works in NES, SNES, PlayStation and PlayStation 2 rooms. It's off unless the host ticks it
3DS online rooms are password-protected when everyone in the room has this version
Instant replay for N64 games can be turned off in Settings
improved: Your per-game settings and cheat choices now follow you to your other PCs
If you use your own Cemu, a newer Wii U save from your other PC is now applied, and your current save is backed up first
Rooms stop you before the game starts if a friend has a different region or version of the same Game Boy, GBA, NES, SNES or DS game
If a friend's copy of the game or emulator differs from the host's, they get a clear message instead of joining and breaking the match
In 3 and 4 player online games, one player leaving no longer cuts everyone else off, and N64 matches keep going for the others
Play and Play Online are greyed out with a short reason while any game or online session is running
Dolphin and Azahar always run in English, so online setup works on any Windows language
Controllers page: hold B for a second to cancel "press a button"
You can react to chat messages with a controller
If RetroAchievements sign-in fails, your cheats and resume point still work, and the game tells you hardcore is off
A second PC with a differently named game file keeps the game's clock and PlayStation memory card 2
fixed: Save states you delete no longer come back from the cloud
A Wi-Fi blip or leaving the room page no longer freezes a GameCube online match
A room host can no longer make your PC load an emulator file from somewhere else on disk
If Azahar can't join a 3DS room you get a clear message instead of silently playing offline
Joining a room with a moved game file now says it can't find the file
The Wii U remote play banner shows the real host's name, and every guest's controller connects even if someone left before the start
Online games ignore packets that pretend to come from another player or the host, and one player can no longer kick others from an N64 match
Closing Cheats from the in-game menu returns you to your game
Windows notifications for invites never appear over a running game
A game you hid no longer shows up greyed out as a friend's game
Turning every cheat off for a game now sticks and syncs
Very big libraries no longer risk a room join message that is too large

versions.title: Fritchii for Ocarina of Time
new: Switch games can now play with Fritchii, Frizti's Ocarina of Time version of Lichii. Pick it in Settings › Switch ("Switch games play with") or for one game in its Settings tab. Lichii stays the default

RetroHub downloads a copy of Fritchii built by GitHub from Frizti's published source and keeps it in its own folder. Your keys, firmware and shader cache are copied over from Lichii the first time you play with it
improved: Your Switch saves follow you between Lichii and Fritchii: before a game starts, RetroHub brings over the newest save and backs up the one it replaces first

versions.title: A new carousel
new: The Cases view has a new carousel: the game you pick stands front and centre, its disc or cartridge slides out after a moment, the games beside it turn to show their covers, and the background glows in the cover's colours
A details panel under the carousel shows the console, play time, a short description, a screenshot when there is one, and Play, Details, Flip and Favorite buttons
improved: Prefer the old shelf of spines? Open the Cases menu and set Style to Classic shelf

versions.title: Real-looking Switch 2 cases
improved: Switch 2 games in the Cases view now look like real Switch 2 boxes: one wide red banner with NINTENDO SWITCH 2 across the top, and the game's art filling the cover instead of a small framed picture
Switch games that only have a square icon show it across the whole width of the case, with its colours blending softly into the bottom of the cover

versions.title: Preload every shader on Switch
new: Switch games can load every shader Lichii has cached when the game starts, so there are fewer hitches while you play (Settings: Shaders at start). Auto turns it on for PCs with 32 GB of RAM or more

versions.title: Ocarina of Time is back on Lichii
improved: Ocarina of Time (Switch 2) plays with Lichii again by default. Hookshot is still there to try: build it on the game's page, then pick it with one button there or in the game's Settings (Plays with)

Lichii is updated to build 95: plants and flowers that used to fade or go missing are drawn again, and it fixes white flashes when the camera moves, the Z-target reticle, Gerudo Valley shaders and a random crash
RetroHub now updates Lichii for you: the next time you play a Switch game it offers the new build, and your keys, firmware, saves and settings stay exactly as they are

versions.title: Ocarina of Time runs natively
new: Ocarina of Time (Switch 2) plays with Hookshot, a native PC version of the game: no emulator, a higher frame rate, and your save carries over
Build Hookshot from the game's page with one button: RetroHub makes it on your PC from your own copy of the game (about 45 minutes, paused while you play)
improved: Your Ocarina of Time save is shared between Hookshot and Lichii, so you can switch either way at any time (the game's Settings: Plays with)
Everything the Hookshot build downloads comes from the official sources and is checked against a fixed fingerprint before it is used

versions.title: Truer cases, smoother Home
new: All Games stands out: the switch is a bright cyan-to-pink pill on every page
improved: Home scrolls smoothly: the mouse wheel always moves the page, even over the side-scrolling rows (swipe sideways or use Shift+wheel to scroll a row), and the controller eases to the row you move to

Cases look like the real thing: DS cases are black, 3DS white, Switch cases clear with the red sleeve (Switch 2 red), and N64, SNES, NES and Game Boy boxes are printed in the game's colours on the sides, flaps and back
Covers: friends' games show full case art where it exists, Pokemon X and Phantom Hourglass get their full cover scans, and covers that were missing are looked up again
The small print on drawn back covers is crisp (labels no longer lose strokes)
fixed: Master Quest shows its own box instead of Ocarina of Time's
Games you own no longer appear a second time in the Friends section

versions.title: Xbox controllers work in Switch games
fixed: Switch: an Xbox controller now works in Lichii right away, with no setup (RetroHub writes the controller the way Lichii sees it, and fixes an old mapping on its own)

versions.title: Real game cases, front to back
new: The Cases view is now the Library's default. If you were on the old default (Grid) you are moved to Cases once; pick any other layout and it stays
Cases show the whole real cover scan: no more banner drawn over the art or covers cut off at the top (DS games lost theirs), and each case takes the shape of its cover
GameCube, Wii U, DS and 3DS games show their real spine and back cover (full cover scans from GameTDB)
Every other game gets a spine and back cover drawn like that console's real ones: real screenshots of the game, its description, developer and publisher, players, an age rating box and a barcode
Descriptions for every game in your library, fetched quietly in the background (Wikipedia, GameTDB), or a short factual line when none exists
Switch 2 games in .nup files use the game's own artwork on a red Switch case
Switch games: a Frame pacing setting. Steady 30 or 60 fps for even, stutter-free motion, or Smooth 60 (a steady 30 doubled by frame generation)
improved: Favourites get a gold star on the case's spine instead of a dot over the cover art
Inspect a case to see its top and bottom too: plastic edges on game cases, folded flaps on cardboard boxes
Small text on case backs is sharper
A library that only shows friends' games has an Add your own games button

versions.title: Cases view, sorting and faster Switch games
new: Cases view: every console's games now come in their own real-world packaging. Black GameCube and PS2 cases, blue Wii U cases, PS1 jewel cases with the black side strip, slim red Switch cases (with a two-tone banner for Switch 2), near-square DS and 3DS cases, tall PSP cases, and cardboard boxes for NES, SNES, N64 and the Game Boy family
New sort orders for the whole library: release year and console, plus a reverse option (Z to A, oldest first) and a favorites-first toggle
Cases view: a Sort button at the top right (O on the keyboard, right stick left or right on a pad)
Cases view: a scrubber bar along the bottom with letter, year or console marks and your position (like 123 / 2,400). Click or drag it to travel
Cases view: jump to the previous or next letter, year or console with LT / RT or Page Up / Page Down, and Home / End for the first and last game
Cases view: a quick-jump rail (J, or right stick up or down) where you pick a letter, year or console, or type the start of a title

Switch games: new per-game settings for GPU accuracy (Low by default, about a third more fps in Ocarina of Time) and asynchronous shaders (on by default, less stutter the first time something new appears)
improved: Cases view: the stage takes its colour from the selected game's cover, with a spotlight, floor reflections and a gentle idle float
Cases view: a bigger title with the console, year, players and genre, plus when you last played and for how long
Cases view: the console tabs show game counts and slide a highlight to the active console, and Switch has its own tab
Cases view: holding a direction speeds up much more, so even a very large library takes seconds to cross, and a big letter shows where you are
Cases view: the back of a case is laid out like the real thing, with pictures, a short description and fine print
fixed: Cases view: a flipped or inspected case no longer slides under the tabs or into the cases next to it
Cases view: Switch games showed a plain dark case labelled "?"
Switch keys and firmware window: the Firmware .zip button no longer runs off the edge of the window

versions.title: Switch 2 .nup games
fixed: Switch 2 games packed as a .nup file (Lichii's own game package) now show up in your library, with their real title and the SWITCH 2 badge. They need no keys
Add Games now accepts Switch and Switch 2 files (.nsp, .xci, .nsz, .xcz, .nro and .nup)

versions.title: Nintendo Switch and Switch 2
new: Nintendo Switch and Switch 2 games: .nsp, .xci, .nsz, .xcz and .nro files, plus Switch 2 game dumps (an exefs folder with main + main.npdm), are listed under a new Switch console. Switch 2 games get a SWITCH 2 badge
They play through Lichii build 88, a very experimental Switch 2 emulator, downloaded the first time you start a Switch game (about 110 MB)

Keys and firmware: RetroHub never includes them. Copy your own once (a prod.keys file and a firmware folder or .zip dumped from your Switch), or copy them in one click from Eden, yuzu, Ryujinx, Citron, Suyu or Sudachi if one is already on this PC
Per-game Switch settings: resolution, VSync and Lichii's FSR3 frame generation (2x turns a 30 fps game into 60 fps)
Your Switch saves go into the save vault and follow you to every PC, like every other console
Switch boot animation, game card and start-up chime
improved: Settings > Games defaults: every console is in the list again (SNES was missing)
fixed: Lichii build 88 can stay running after you close its window; RetroHub now ends it after 15 seconds so your save is copied and the next game can start

versions.title: Cases view
new: Cases view: All Games can show your games as 3D cases in a full-screen carousel, with console tabs, smooth scrolling and reflections on a glossy floor
Flip and Inspect: flip a case to see its back (description, info and your own screenshots), or pick it up and turn it with the right stick
Shuffle: spin the carousel to a random game
Each console gets its own case: plastic cases for disc and card systems, cardboard boxes for cartridge games
TV mode can open straight into the Cases view (Settings > General)

versions.title: Your account survives a reinstall
new: Already have an account: the waiting and blocked screens can sign you in to your existing account
improved: Reinstalling: RetroHub keeps a backup of your account outside its folder, so a reinstall picks your account back up instead of making a new one
Reinstalling: the installer now offers the folder RetroHub already runs from, so it updates that copy in place
Antivirus: online helper scripts now run through a small RetroHub helper, which should mean fewer false alarms

versions.title: Link your consoles, bring your saves
new: Transfer Pak: Pokemon Stadium 1 and 2, Mario Golf, Mario Tennis and Perfect Dark can use a Game Boy game from your library, with its save backed up and synced
Game Boy Advance link: connect a GBA to Pokemon Colosseum, XD, Four Swords Adventures, Crystal Chronicles, the Tingle Tuner and Metroid Prime (needs your own GBA BIOS)
Pal Park: put a GBA game in the DS's GBA slot so Diamond, Pearl, Platinum, HeartGold and SoulSilver can bring Pokemon over
Bring your saves: import saves from RetroArch, Project64, Dolphin, PCSX2, mGBA, VisualBoyAdvance and melonDS, with a preview and automatic backups
Verify my games: checks your cartridge games against known good dumps, plus a Library health card for bad dumps, missing BIOS, offline folders and duplicates
Smart shelves: shelves that fill themselves from a rule (console, genre, players, status, favorites, not played lately, decade)
Progress: mark games as playing, beaten, 100%, dropped or backlog and add a short note; it syncs between your PCs
N64 resume: N64 games continue where you left off
Which save: when another PC has a newer save, you choose which one to start from
Display: RetroHub reopens on the same monitor and spot, with an Open on choice, a UI size slider (80-200%) and Reduce motion
Blocked people: a list in Settings with Unblock
improved: Sync: renames, covers, notes and status from different PCs now merge game by game instead of overwriting each other
Saves: imported saves, history restores and folder pulls go to your cloud saves right away
Library: the toolbar wraps cleanly at large UI sizes, and scrolling big libraries is smoother
Friends: when sign-in stops working, the panel says what to do next
N64: save and load states confirm the core finished, and a failed save no longer wipes the old state
fixed: Your own messages no longer show twice after a restart
Cover art retries after a network hiccup instead of staying blank
The library scan no longer follows folder junctions
A cancelled PlayStation add no longer leaves a half-copied game behind
Adding a game no longer re-reads your whole library
Moving RetroHub to a monitor with a different scale rescales it

versions.title: Shelves, Continue and a bigger Discover
new: 3D shelf view: your games as cartridges, discs and cases on wooden shelves; the one you pick slides out to show its cover
Continue where you left off: Home shows your last game's save picture with a big Continue button and a Jump back in row
Bigger Discover: about 1,100 picks (up to ~100 per console), Show more, and the full catalog of every known game for older consoles
Sort and filter Discover: by title, year or players; filter by genre, players, decade or what you own, and search
Welcome back: a quick look at what's new the first time you open RetroHub after an update
improved: Discover: an All consoles view mixes every console's best picks together

versions.title: Invite codes and quick approvals
new: Invite codes: the owner makes a code in Admin and sends it; a new friend types it on the waiting screen (or opens the invite link) and gets in at once
Admin: people waiting for approval are listed first with big Approve / Deny buttons, plus Approve by friend code
Owner notifications: "<name> wants to join" with Approve / Deny right in the bell, and a note when an invite is used
improved: Floating invite cards hide while the bell or a pop-up is open
fixed: A new account could drop its connection right after starting and wait a minute to reconnect

versions.title: Smash online needs an account too
new: Smash Classic online now checks your RetroHub account: banned or waiting accounts can't join Smash rooms
improved: With 'Only approved accounts can join rooms' on, Smash rooms are covered as well
fixed: Smash online shows the server's reason when a room refuses you instead of a generic connection error

versions.title: Only people you approve
new: Banned accounts and accounts waiting for approval see only a lock screen: no library, no games, not even offline
New accounts now wait for the owner's approval. Everyone who already has RetroHub keeps working
Admin: "Only approved accounts can join rooms" switch for lobbies, game rooms and spectating
improved: The waiting screen shows your name and friend code so the owner knows it's you, with Check again
RetroHub refreshes its shortcut icon after an update, so the new logo shows up in the Start Menu and taskbar
fixed: Server busy in a room is now a short retry instead of an error

versions.title: Owner tools and a tidier room
new: Owner-only Admin page: see accounts, ban people you don't recognise, and optionally require approval for new accounts. Existing friends are never affected
improved: Room page: the room code bar and Leave room stay visible in small windows; long reasons wrap instead of being cut off
Invite cards shrink while a menu or pop-up is open so they no longer cover buttons
Party votes always show their Close button; the podium and cheats strip look tidier
Checkboxes are easier to see in every theme; the Host and Join cards are the same height
fixed: The sidebar could say "Connecting" while you were already in a room

versions.title: New look, Discover, and every player on the controller
new: Discover tab: highly rated games for every console, with Play, Install (from your shared packs) or Add your own copy
Library views: List, Compact and Showcase next to the usual Grid, plus an A-Z strip and right-stick letter jumps for big libraries
Friend profiles: head-to-head record, last played together, top games and games you both own. The friend menu is now short and tidy
Change your controls while a game is running: built-in emulators pick up the new buttons straight away (Dolphin, Cemu, PCSX2, Azahar and PPSSPP on the next launch)
New Candy D-pad logo and app icon
improved: Room page redesigned: the game pick and Launch at the top, one compact row per player, the room code and a red Leave room at the bottom
Party mode is a single slim bar; its setup and standings open in pop-ups
You can keep browsing and changing settings in RetroHub while a game runs
Menu sounds are now off by default (turn them on in Settings > General)
Games you can't use are listed under Settings > files need attention with the reason, instead of vanishing
fixed: Same-PC multiplayer in NES, SNES and PS1 games only listened to controller 1; every controller now drives its own player
NES players 3-4 never reached the game, even with the Four Score on
PS2 (Gauntlet and others), GameCube, Wii U and PSP could give a player the wrong controller or none when pads were unplugged or reordered
Online NES and SNES ignored each player's own button mapping
Archives with Mac leftover files, accented or Japanese names, generic names like game.iso, .gcz, PS2 .cso and multi-disc sets now install and get the right title
Long game titles and labels no longer run under buttons on the room and friends screens

versions.title: GameCube online stays in sync
fixed: GameCube online: friends who joined a room started with an empty memory card while the host played on their real save, so games like Super Mario Strikers, Mario Superstar Baseball and Mario Party 6 drifted apart a few seconds in. Everyone now starts on the host's save for that session (the host's save is the only one written)

versions.title: PS2 online: everyone can play
fixed: PS2 online: only player 1's controller worked in game; players 2-4 couldn't join (for example at Gauntlet's character select)

versions.title: PS2 BIOS found in more places
fixed: A PS2 BIOS inside a folder in your games folder (like Games\PS2\ps2Bios\...) was not found, so PS2 online said "Your PC has no PlayStation 2 BIOS"

versions.title: PS2 online for 4 players
new: PlayStation 2 online rooms now take up to 4 players (multitap), for games that support it
fixed: PS2 online could not start: "The PlayStation 2 online core could not be downloaded: download has the wrong size". The core now comes from RetroHub's own pinned copy, so upstream updates can't break it

versions.title: GameCube online at full speed
improved: GameCube online now passes game traffic along the moment it arrives instead of once per screen refresh, cutting the delay it added from about 50 ms to under 5 ms
Super Mario Strikers online is back on one CPU core: the slowdown was never the core setting, and one core keeps players in sync
fixed: Mario Superstar Baseball, Super Mario Strikers and other GameCube games ran at about half speed online with friends far away. The input buffer is now set from your real ping before the game starts and follows it during play (tested at 100% speed with a 180 ms ping, directly and through the relay)

versions.title: Smoother GameCube online
improved: GameCube online picks its input buffer from your connection instead of a fixed small one, so games stop stuttering while they wait for the other player
Super Mario Strikers online uses both CPU cores, like Mario Superstar Baseball

versions.title: Everything is back, and 4-player online is fixed
new: All of 1.30 and 1.31 is back: party mode, brackets, ROM hacks, PSP, friend challenges, Discord, Ctrl+K search and the rest
fixed: 3-4 player online games (N64 and GameCube) froze or drifted out of sync because the online server limited each room's traffic too tightly; the limit is raised
Mario Golf, Mario Tennis and Pokemon Stadium no longer drift out of sync online with several players
Includes the earlier fixes again: PS2 cue/bin games, playing right after an install, doubled friends' games and Mario Superstar Baseball online speed

versions.title: Back to the steady version while online gets fixed
fixed: Online games with 3-4 players (N64 and GameCube) could freeze or drift out of sync after the last updates. This update brings RetroHub back to version 1.29.24, which played them well, while the problem is fixed. The newer features return in the next update

versions.title: PSP, friend challenges and a lot of convenience
new: PlayStation Portable: add your PSP games (ISO, CSO, CHD, PBP) and play them; PPSSPP downloads itself the first time, saves follow you to your other PCs
Send a screenshot to a friend from the screenshot viewer
Friend challenges: from the game menu, challenge a friend to beat the exact moment you're at, with a timer and a little leaderboard
Send a ROM hack to a friend so you can play it together online
Discord: show what you're playing on your Discord profile (off until you turn it on)
Find anything: just start typing, or press Ctrl+K for a search box that finds games, friends, settings and actions
Connection test in Settings > Online, and Copy diagnostics in the new Help tab
